Answer: B
Reason: The imaging sequence demonstrates initial bilateral opacities (Figure 1) progressing to dense, diffuse consolidations (Figure 4), which is characteristic of severe alveolar hemorrhage seen in Weil Syndrome (severe leptospirosis). The subsequent images (Figures 5a and 5b) show complete radiological resolution, a known outcome for pulmonary involvement in Weil Syndrome with appropriate management, distinguishing it from the other options.
